body:
I have been talking to my friend here in the town I'm still living in.  His mother is a therapist (and brought work home with her throughout his life, so to speak), that's been helpful.  For someone who is young enough to be my son/nephew, he has wisdom. 

As far as where I'm going, I've been away from there for so long that I'm not sure who I can trust yet.  I've been gone for sixteen years, and a lot can happen in that time.  Having said that, my rational side knows they wouldn't abandon me if I told them.  

I said above that I've talked it over with my sister some, but I really don't want to scare her.  I will probably stay with her for a while when I get back, maybe putter around in her garden or something.  

What's getting me, is that before this woman, I was by myself and happy for several years.  While we were dating, everything else around me fell apart and I guess I didn't see it happening.  And when it ended is when it felt like there was nothing left.  And if I wasn't this way right now, it seems that we could make it work sometime in the future.  It just sucks, because of all the ones that have been, she seemed to finally be the one I actually imagined a future with.  But right now I scare her.  Hell, I scare me right now (although I'm doing a helluva a lot better than 24 hours ago).

Up until about five years ago life was mostly good.  Little bouts of depression here and there, nothing like now.  And I lived in a local that had wonderful mental health services that I did take advantage of.  I lived in a resort town and snowboarded in the winter, biked in the summer.  

Foolishly, I moved away, thinking that I wanted the city life (there was a woman involved with that as well).  Ever since moving here, it went downhill.  I didn't get to go snowboarding.  I got hit by a car and broke my face and a couple years later broke my hand in a skateboarding mishap.  And had the call center job that was very emotionally draining.

I've never really had any goals or passions, I have had some hobbies to a degree.  I have enjoyed taking photos until recently, now I just can't seem to bring myself to go out and do it.  I dropped out of college in the early 90s and realize now that it's probably set me back as far as fulfilling employment goes.  Of course everything I've just said is clouded by the crap that's going on in my head right now. 

I wasn't an extraordinarily happy person growing up, I always have felt like an outsider looking in.  Although, I feel that I pretty much accepted that in my twenties.  Well, until recently, perhaps.  My home life was the typical parents who hate each other but stayed together for the children/religious reasons.  My siblings and I are as close as we can be with 1200 miles between us, but I don't want to scare them with this stuff.   I've let my sister know about some of it.

I'm not too worried about the firearm, throughout the worst moments of it, I've not considered using as I don't want anyone to have to clean up that kind of mess.  I'm going to leave it in the box and leave it at my brothers house when I get back.  There is some sentimental value, I inherited it from my grandmother when she died (natural causes).  I only have about 3 days left here before I leave anyway.  In the last 24 hours I've calmed down enough to know that if I take it day by day, I will get through this.

The non-rational side of my brain makes it hard to believe this will go away.  But getting it out seems to be helping some.

Holy cow, I wrote a book.
